new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (3 pp., native text; the PDF's metadata gives the Title 'OPD', Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 2004-08-23, footer 'Kalo (Keapara) OPD Printed: August 24, 2004'). extracted text gives, after the vowel/diphthong chart, exactly: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' / 'Stress is on penultima.' followed by 'Syllable Patterns V / VV / CV / CVV' with examples (e 'yes', ai 'us,we', nu.pa 'wet', goi 'you sg.', kui.ta..), empty 'Conventions' headings, a transcribed passage, and 'Bibliography: Laeka, Ali 1975. Kalo Phonology. Ms, UPNG, SIL Ukarumpa.' So the quote is verbatim at the stated locator. The statement is a bare one-liner with no stress-marked examples, no secondary stress, no excep…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Kalo (Keapara) falls on the penultimate syllable; syllables are all open (V, VV, CV, CVV).
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned; the sheet gives no stress-marked examples and is flagged 'Data checked by: (needs checking!)'.
new_statements.domain_note: One-line generalisation on an SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet, presumably word-level citation forms; how VV/CVV (diphthong) syllables count for 'penultima' is not stated. Consistent with Short 1938's incidental Keapara forms po'raha, vi'roho (penultimate) versus Hula po'ra, vi'ro.
new_statements.identity_note: The stress statement is for the Kalo dialect (Glottolog kalo1259, Kalo village at the mouth of the Kemp Welch River), which Ethnologue/Glottolog file under Keapara [khz] but whose speakers regard it as a language distinct from Keapara (Laeka 1989: 5; King 2014 archive description). The OPD header reads 'Kalo (Keapara) Language [KHZ]'. Nothing first-hand was found for the Aroma, Maopa, Hula-side or Keapara (Kerepunu) dialects beyond Short 1938's incidental Keapara forms po'raha, vi'roho (penultimate). Hula (hula1239) is a separate Glottolog language: Dutton 1970: 889 ('stress is phonemic and related to syllable length') and Short 1938 p. 5 describe Hula, not Keapara proper.
